![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14209228/assets/bc7e248783ccf6b1eda95a1c2c80300e48d8cdb48f39ea07296ed3bf51bfaa29.png)

A small, circular puddle evaporates on a floor. If the puddle’s area is decreasing at a rate of $32\pi \,{\text{cm}}^{2}/\text{min},$ calculate the rate of change of its circumference at the moment when the radius is $8\,\text{cm}.$ Do not round the answer.

The circumference of the puddle is decreasing at a rate of 
{{field-1}} $\text{cm}/\text{min}.$
question.worked_solution:
In this situation, we want to find $\frac{\text{d}C}{\text{d}t}$ at the moment when $r=8,$ and we are also told that  $\frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t}=-32\pi .$

To start, let's set up an equation relating the area $A$ and the circumference $C$ of the circle. Since $C=2\pi r$ and $A=\pi {r}^{2},$ the relationship between $A$ and $C$ is

$$
A=\pi {r}^{2}=\pi {(\frac{C}{2\pi })}^{2}=\frac{{C}^{2}}{4\pi }.
$$

Differentiating this relationship with respect to $t$ using implicit differentiation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(A) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{{C}^{2}}{4\pi }) \\ \frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}C}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}C}(\frac{{C}^{2}}{4\pi }) \\ \frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}C}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{C}{2\pi }.\end{aligned}
$$

When $r=8\,\text{cm},$ $C=2\pi (8)=16\pi \text{ cm}.$ Hence, substituting $\frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t}=-32\pi $ and $C=16\pi ,$ and solving for $\frac{\text{d}C}{\text{d}t}.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}-32\pi  & =\frac{\text{d}C}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{16\pi }{2\pi } \\ -32\pi  & =\frac{\text{d}C}{\text{d}t}\cdot 8 \\ \frac{\text{d}C}{\text{d}t} & =-4\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

We conclude that the circumference is decreasing at a rate of $4\pi \text{ cm}\text{/min}.$
